open_points.subject: functions.add_trial_case authored file fixtures
open_points.text: Inputs: A contract version, input values by port, optional expected outputs, the actor. / A check is given a file as facts — digest, size, media type — never bytes. / put_value_bytes requires: Bytes and their expected digest and size.
open_points.question: How does an authored trial case supply the actual bytes of a file input or expected file output so functions can persist and later execute the fixture?
options: Carry file bytes alongside their declared facts in add_trial_case
Use a separate prior upload/reference operation
Forbid authored file fixtures and allow only captured ones
open_points.default_guess: Carry each fixture's bytes alongside its digest, size and media type, validate them, then publish them with put_value_bytes.

open_points.subject: functions.try_implementation result
open_points.text: Outputs: One TrialExecution per case in corpus order: outcome, output digests, pass or output_mismatch. / Records reach a caller as they are, with values resolved by module:surface: a value StoredValue as its JSON content.
open_points.question: Does try_implementation return successful value outputs as resolved JSON values, or only their digests?
options: Return resolved JSON values subject to disclosure masking
Return digests only
Return both values and digests
open_points.default_guess: Return the TrialExecution records with resolved JSON values where disclosure permits, plus the stored digests; return only file facts for files.

open_points.subject: approval request_digest
open_points.text: The request_digest is the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of that description. / Build one request ... with its description and request_digest.
open_points.question: What exact JSON structure and field names constitute the request description whose canonical JSON is hashed?
options: A fixed object schema with named method, URL, headers and body-description fields
A fixed ordered tuple or array schema
An implementation-private representation that merely contains the listed facts
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned fixed JSON object schema, with headers and multipart parts represented as ordered arrays.

open_points.subject: EffectAttempt idempotency_key
open_points.text: The EffectAttempt's idempotency_key is the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of those fields' values.
open_points.question: Is the hashed value an object keyed by field name, an ordered list of values, or an ordered list of name/value pairs?
options: Object mapping key-field names to values
Values array in manifest order
Name/value-pair array in manifest order
open_points.default_guess: Hash an ordered array of name/value pairs in the manifest's declared field order.

open_points.subject: manifest_source revision access
open_points.text: The kernel reads a service's record only from <manifest_location>/<service_id>.json at the configured manifest_revision. / manifest_source returns the manifest location and revision fixed at start.
open_points.question: How is a file read 'at' manifest_revision: is the location already an immutable checkout, does bindings invoke a version-control reader, or does the revision select a directory or snapshot by another rule?
options: manifest_location is an already checked-out immutable snapshot and revision is verified metadata
The kernel reads the file directly from a version-control object at the named revision
The revision selects a snapshot directory under manifest_location
open_points.default_guess: Read through a read-only version-control operation at the exact configured revision without changing the working tree.

open_points.subject: media_type comparison across ports and fixtures
open_points.text: An edge requires both ports to carry ... for files, the same media type. / for a file, the schema check is its media type against the port's. / A response Content-Type is compared on type and subtype without regard to case and ignoring parameters.
open_points.question: Outside HTTP response validation, are media types compared as exact strings or as case-insensitive type/subtype values with parameters normalized or forbidden?
options: Exact string equality
Case-insensitive type/subtype equality while ignoring parameters
Canonicalize media types when authored and compare the canonical form
open_points.default_guess: Require parameter-free media types, canonicalize type and subtype to lowercase, and compare the canonical form.

open_points.subject: HTTP Content-Encoding response handling
open_points.text: The kernel asks for no content encoding (Accept-Encoding: identity); the size counted is the response body's bytes after transfer decoding.
open_points.question: If a service nevertheless returns Content-Encoding such as gzip, does the kernel reject it, preserve the encoded bytes, or decode it before size and output validation?
options: Reject any non-identity Content-Encoding as a malformed response
Do not content-decode; validate the encoded bytes
Decode supported content encodings before counting and validation
open_points.default_guess: Reject a non-identity Content-Encoding so HTTP-client automatic decompression cannot change the observed body.

open_points.subject: failure_detail representation and masking length
open_points.text: At most failure_detail_bytes_max of [an error body] is kept as failure_detail. / A failure_detail ... is returned to an agent only as its length and that class.
open_points.question: How are arbitrary non-UTF-8 error-body bytes represented as failure_detail, and is the masked length measured in original bytes, retained UTF-8 bytes, or characters?
options: Store a bounded byte string and report its byte length
Decode UTF-8 strictly and omit invalid bodies
Decode with replacement, store bounded UTF-8 text and report its UTF-8 byte length
open_points.default_guess: Decode with UTF-8 replacement, truncate at a character boundary to the byte ceiling, and report the retained UTF-8 byte length.

open_points.subject: store.spool_file rollback of an attempt
open_points.text: A refusal keeps nothing of that file or of any file that attempt spooled before. / A link or an I/O failure is internal_error with nothing kept of that file.
open_points.question: If removing files previously spooled by the same attempt fails while handling a ceiling refusal, what result is returned, what partial files may remain, and how are those files excluded from later spool-ceiling accounting?
options: Return internal_error and stop, leaving any remnants as unreadable unrecorded files to be replaced on recovery
Still return refused and defer cleanup to startup
Make the attempt's spool publication atomic so either every file or none becomes visible
open_points.default_guess: Return internal_error, expose no SpooledFile records, stop the kernel, and replace or remove all unrecorded files at those attempt positions during recovery.
